In mathematics, the '''Lie operad''' is an [[operad theory|operad]] [[Operad algebra|whose algebras]] are [[Lie algebra]]s. The notion (at least one version) was introduced by {{harvtxt|Ginzburg|Kapranov|1994}}<ref>{{citation |last1=Ginzburg |first1=Victor |title=Koszul duality for operads |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume=76 |issue=1 |pages=203–272 |year=1994 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-94-07608-4 |mr=1301191 |last2=Kapranov |first2=Mikhail}}</ref> in their formulation of [[Koszul duality]].

== Definition à la Ginzburg–Kapranov ==
Fix a base field ''k'' and let <math>\mathcal{Lie}(x_1, \dots, x_n)</math> denote the [[free Lie algebra]] over ''k'' with generators <math>x_1, \dots, x_n</math> and <math>\mathcal{Lie}(n) \subset \mathcal{Lie}(x_1, \dots, x_n)</math> the subspace spanned by all the bracket monomials containing each <math>x_i</math> exactly once. The [[symmetric group]] <math>S_n</math> acts on <math>\mathcal{Lie}(x_1, \dots, x_n)</math> by permutations of the generators and, under that action, <math>\mathcal{Lie}(n)</math> is invariant. The operadic composition is given by substituting expressions (with renumbered variables) for variables. Then, <math>\mathcal{Lie} = \{ \mathcal{Lie}(n) \}</math> is an operad.<ref>{{harvnb|Ginzburg|Kapranov|1994|loc=§ 1.3.9.}}</ref>

== Koszul-Dual ==
The [[Koszul-dual]] of <math>\mathcal{Lie}</math> is the [[commutative-ring operad]], an operad whose algebras are the commutative rings over ''k.''
